reports.title: Target Corporation Reports Third Quarter Earnings

lines: •Full-year net sales growth in a range around 6 percent, one percentage point higher than the prior guidance range.
Additionally, building on the strong returns generated by capital investments in 2026, the Company expects to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in capital expenditures in 2027.

desk.headline: Sales up 7.1% to $27.1bn and EPS $2.65, both beat; full-year sales and EPS outlook raised

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (equal to diluted GAAP this quarter)

results: Net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1bn; comparable sales grew 5.6%, driven by 5.0% more transactions.
Hardlines (Fun 101) sales jumped about 27% and beauty rose 9%, but apparel slipped 4%.
EPS of $2.65 compared with $1.78 adjusted a year ago; $0.50 came from IEEPA tariff refunds, so underlying adjusted EPS rose about 21%.
Gross margin widened to 30.5% from 28.2%; about 1.1 points of that was the tariff refund.
Paid $527m in dividends and bought back $251m of stock; quarterly capex rose to $1.4bn on new and remodelled stores.

guidance.summary: Target lifted its 2026 outlook again: net sales growth of around 6% (was around 5%) and EPS of $10.65–11.40 (was $9.90–10.90), including about $2.14 of refunds received so far. It plans $5–6bn of capex in 2027.

points: Sales cooled somewhat in October but picked up again in November, running in line with plan so far.
Value remains the focus: prices were cut on thousands of items and hundreds of apparel items are being repriced lower.
Higher freight and fuel costs partly offset margin gains; tariff refunds were described as a one-off boost.
Apparel, especially women's fashion and shoes, is weak, and home is seen as a multi-year turnaround.
Q4 buybacks are expected at a similar level to Q3; strong store returns underpin the higher 2027 capex plan.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — The Singju Post, 18 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (19 Aug 2026)

watch: Holiday-season sales and whether November's pick-up holds through December.
Margins without tariff refunds as freight and fuel costs stay high.
Progress in weak apparel and home categories.
